speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head J of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The past year has been marked by disruption and change on a global scale.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has exacerbated some worrying geopolitical trends and seen the rise of growing nationalism across the world.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In the face of a serious public health crisis and economic challenges on a scale not experienced in recent years, many countries have turned inwards and shifted their focus to domestic priorities.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They have closed their borders and put in place a multitude of protectionist policies.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This pandemic has paradoxically weakened the prospects for multilateral cooperation at a time where it is needed the most.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Even the distribution of much needed vaccines across the world has become yet another area of great power contestation.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Small states like Singapore are particularly vulnerable to external geopolitical shifts, and a volatile and complex international environment would invariably undermine our own security.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As geopolitical rivalries intensify and as countries' commitment to multilateralism becomes increasingly undermined by the pandemic, Singapore is unfortunately put in a challenging position.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In light of these tumultuous times, how have recent geopolitical and security developments shaped the Ministry of Defence and the Singapore Armed Forces plans and priorities, both now and in the years ahead?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: On average, that would mean an air threat almost every day.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Defence of our country is of fundamental importance.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: It extends beyond air defence and concerns our ability to effectively and safely deal with external threats and to safeguard our survivor.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: It is only when Singapore is secure and safe, that Singaporeans can live our lives and pursue our aspirations with peace of mind.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: COVID-19 has certainly caused unprecedented disruption to our economy, society and our very way of life.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Over the last 12 months, Singaporeans have lived with closed borders, the circuit breaker, and the introduction of numerous limits on everything from work modalities to our social gatherings.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: I, for one, remember trying to balance a Zoom meeting with three other separate home-based learning sessions at the same time.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: In this time of crisis, Singaporeans have risen as one to face down the virus.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: The Government, civil servants, frontline workers and ordinary Singaporeans have all done their part to bring us to where we are today – to be able to enjoy some semblance of normalcy.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Many may have heard or read about how MINDEF and SAF has contributed to the national COVID-19 fight.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: But few know the full scale of the problem that we faced, and the might that MINDEF and SAF brought to bear against it, especially when the crisis was at its peak.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Seeing the SAF trucks roll in to our Community Club with the first delivery of surgical mask many months ago, was a moment of pride.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: For all these and more, I add my gratitude to our servicemen and women for your stellar contributions.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Would the Minister for Defence share more details of MINDEF and SAF's contributions to Singapore's efforts against COVID-19, including on-going and future plans?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Mr Chairman, in many parts of the world, the global pandemic caused by COVID-19 has weakened public confidence in Government's capacity to respond to threats to public health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In Singapore COVID-19 has disrupted our way of life, although have thus far, have been able to mitigate and contained the impact.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: When the crisis is over, many countries will need to better prepare for the next pandemic including new biological threats.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Given our collective experiences over the past year, many now agree that global health issues can and will have an impact on national security.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Can the Minister for Defence share with us what MINDEF is doing to strengthen our defence against future pandemics and other potential biological threats?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore faces threats around the clock and this does not change with COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: As a small nation, we know it takes very little to tip us over.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: This is why we need the Singapore Armed Forces to be ready at all times.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: I would imagine that this has affected the RSAF in particular, which requires sufficient air space to conduct its flight training.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Yet, it is imperative that the SAF continue to maintain vigilance over all of our air, land, sea and cyber domains – to defend our sovereignty.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Over the long term, how does the SAF intend to manage the challenges of a prolonged pandemic?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Chairman, the need for both diplomacy and deterrence is well understood by Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The Workers' Party believes in a strong defence.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have also personally served on MINDEF's ACCORD Committee for seven years and found it very meaningful.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This can be seen from Parliamentary Questions filed by various Members of Parliament who represent constituents living proximate to air bases.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Residents from Aljunied GRC are in this group, living close to Paya Lebar Air Base.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have tried to explain that the RSAF needs to train in the darkness as well, but some insist that the current levels are excessive.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: To be fair, there have also been studies about aircraft noise being associated with detrimental effects on health.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For instance, has the COVID-19 pandemic required SAF to do more training locally?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Chairman, in our nation’s fight against COVID-19, MINDEF and SAF personnel have answered the call of duty and taken up critical roles both at the frontline and behind the scenes.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While combating the challenges of the on-going pandemic is at the forefront of our minds, we are also keenly aware that security threats do not abate during this period.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Enlistment, training and operations must go on in the "new normal", in order to maintain a high level of operational readiness that is critical to safeguard Singapore’s peace and security.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our servicemen and women have traditionally lived, trained and operated in close proximity.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The training in the SAF is physically demanding, which could lead to the transmission of droplets.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Besides the risk of transmission in camps, other risks are in confined spaces and they include tanks, aircraft and seacraft.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What about our servicemen and women presently in facilities overseas?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What kind of protection has been put in place for them?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Are there sufficient vaccines and access to the best quality of healthcare for our service personnel abroad?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In addition to preventive measures, would the Ministry also share the measures which will kick in when a serviceman or woman is suspected of having the infection?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How would SAF prevent such situations from escalating?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, around the world, COVID-19 has posed tremendous challenges to governments’ capacity to respond to and manage public health threats.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: In January 2020, COVID-19 emerged in Singapore and rapidly disrupted our way of life.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I am certain it has affected MINDEF or SAF in a number of ways, including having an impact on our NSmen training.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: I note that the SAF has implemented rigorous safe management measures, testing and cohorting regimes.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, if my memory still vivid, MINDEF or SAF have also contributed to the national COVID-19 response to keep our frontline workers safe during the peak of the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: How will MINDEF continue to ensure the safety of NSmen amidst the COVID-19 context?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Mr Chairman, the SAF plays a vital role in deterring potential aggressors and protecting the nation’s peace and stability.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Rapid technological advancements have enabled militaries all over the world to become increasingly capable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The pandemic might have slowed down defence spending but it will certainly rebound.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Countries will not abandon their efforts to modernise their military.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Conflicts continue to flare up globally, both on the battlefields and in the cyberspace.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: As a small country, our military size will always be limited.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Thus, we need to make up for our size with the constant upgrading of SAF’s capabilities to take our nation into the new era of defence.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The Next-Generation SAF vision was first introduced in 2019 by Minister for Defence Dr Ng Eng Hen with the core objective of enabling the nation to better respond to security threats, especially in the new age of technology.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Could MINDEF provide us with an update on the SAF’s progress towards building the Next-Generation SAF to better guard our national interests?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Chairman, the nature of warfare is continually evolving and so must the SAF if it wishes to stay relevant.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: State-on-state conflict may no longer manifest itself in the exchange of physical blows.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Instead, we see conflict existing below the threshold of war and waged in non-physical domains such as the cyber realm.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Threats to national security have become increasingly amorphous and may not easily be defined or identified.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: At the same time, the threat of terrorism remains prevalent.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Terrorist groups in the region and around the world could try to capitalise on existing societal fragmentation exacerbated by COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: The SAF must be able to defend Singapore against a whole range of threats.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: This resource reality means that the SAF cannot go about its business as usual.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: While the national resource pool might be decreasing in numbers, its texture is also changing.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: The new generation of Singaporeans are becoming more educated and digitally literate.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: This places the SAF in a good position to harness the potential offered by digital technology.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: The SAF must be agile and adapt in order to reap the potential that digital technology has to offer.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Could the Minister for Defence provide an update on efforts towards building the Next Generation SAF?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Mr Chairman, our security environment is becoming increasingly complex.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: MINDEF and SAF will need to gear itself up to be operationally ready for a wider spectrum of threats.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: However, at the same time, SAF will be faced with the quantitative challenge of filling manpower due to our declining population growth rate.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Going forward, the conundrum of doing more with a leaner SAF is going to be increasingly pressing issue.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: As a small country, Singapore has always been cognisant that manpower is an inherent constraint.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: We have constantly leveraged technology to supplement our limitations in terms of our manpower.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: The SAF has done so in the past and will continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Could the Minister for Defence please update the House on how MINDEF/SAF is preparing itself to deal with the increasing manpower constraint that it will face?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: Over the last one year, the news headlines have understandably been dominated by the COVID-19 pandemic and US-China relations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: However, we must not be distracted – terrorism is still present.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: When the world is focused on fighting COVID-19, the terrorists could very well be planning their next attacks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: Violent extremism may be closer than imagined, especially with the pandemic shrouding the threat of terrorism.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: We clearly cannot allow fighting terrorism to take a backseat amongst our priorities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: As the world shifts towards a digital one, not only are we plagued by the concern of conventional terrorism, increasingly, that of unconventional ones such as cyberattacks and radicalisation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: The proliferation of various messages platforms which offers anonymity and encryption features also make it easier for terror groups to advance malicious activities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: Mr Chairman, as seen from the aforementioned issues, the threat of terrorism is not only increasing, but evolving as we speak.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: I would be grateful if MINDEF could provide us with an update on how they are maintaining vigilance against terrorist threats, especially in relation to those in cyberspace.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, as part of the MINDEF Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC), I had the chance to visit MINDEF’s impressive cyber-range, which seeks to train our cyberwarriors on how to deal with simulated cyberattacks.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I believe MINDEF has invested considerable resources in the area of cybersecurity.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Nevertheless, this is an area that the threats are increasing exponentially.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: The recent breach experienced by the cybersecurity company FireEye via the company supplier, Solarwinds, that supplied the network monitoring software, demonstrates the heightened risks.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Software supply-chain attacks are some of the hardest type of attacks to prevent because they take advantage of the trusted relationships between vendors and customers and machine-to-machine communication channels, such as software update mechanisms that are inherently trusted by users.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And Solarwinds is not an ordinary software vendor.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Its customers include 425 of Fortune 500 companies, all top ten US telecommunications companies, all top five US accounting firms, all branches of the US Military, the Pentagon and the State Department.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This goes to show that no country, industry, organisation or even type of information technology is immune to cybersecurity threat.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Chairman, at the COS debate last year, the Minister for Defence informed the House about the formation of a NS Review Committee (NSRC) to examine ways to enrich the NS experience and maximise the potential of every national serviceman.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: National Service forms the backbone of our defence.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is also a rite of passage for all young males in Singapore, who commit two years in the prime of their lives to safeguard our territory and ensure our sovereignty and peace.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: When they complete their full-time NS, our servicemen continue to make sacrifices in their personal and work life, so that they are fit and ready to protect Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The requirement to serve up to 40 days of Operationally Ready National Service (ORNS) per year is necessary but demanding.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should seek to minimise the disruption to their civilian routines as much as possible.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Last year, I spoke about supporting our men with care arrangements for their family members in the event they do not have the necessary support when they are in camp.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is an important concern because we need our servicemen to focus on their military duties with peace of mind.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is important that we continue to examine ways to bring the best out of our servicemen through the different stages of their NS journey.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will the Ministry share an update on how SAF can improve upon how it assesses that the unit assigned to an NSF is the best fit for him?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How is SAF tapping upon our serviceman’s vocations and civilian expertise to enhance their NS contributions?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How can our NSF communicate their areas of interest with SAF so that it could be better filtered or sorted into a role that the NSF could excel at?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can more flexibility be exercised so that in the event of poor fit, whether these are functional or manpower incompatibility, redeployment can be made?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In addition, how can SAF motivate NSFs to do better, beyond what they are required to and align the goals of the members of the unit?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Lastly, how will MINDEF engage families and employers to get fuller support and cooperation for our servicemen’s deployments?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is it possible to make better use of new technology to enable our servicemen to manage both NS obligations and civilian duties?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Likewise, let us leverage on technology to enhance SAF communications and interactions with our servicemen.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to take both cuts together.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Much has been said in this House regarding the Singapore Green Plan 2030, which has been described as a whole-of-nation effort to tackle climate change decisively.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: What are MINDEF and SAF doing to advance the sustainability agenda and to support the Singapore Green Plan 2030?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: At the COS debate last year, the Minister for Defence spoke about the various measures taken by MINDEF to improve environmental sustainability and reduce carbon footprint.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: I recognise that this is not an easy balance for MINDEF to strike because our military is organised to function in wartime conditions.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: In war, one of the first things that any capable adversaries will target are supply lines and fuel.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: So, while we get our armed forces to go green, we must bear in mind that operational resilience under the toughest conditions must be achieved.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: It will potentially entail a revamp of our military’s supply chain planning process.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And can MINDEF share its broad planning principles on how to balance contributing to sustainability while maintaining our critical defence edge?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Mr Chairman, apart from protecting Singapore from current threats, MINDEF plays an important role in safeguarding our future.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: At last year’s debate, MINDEF shared about various measures taken by the Ministry to improve environmental sustainability and to reduce carbon emissions.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And that they would take various steps to ensure that the SAF would be on track in meeting our national emission targets.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister to provide an update on how MINDEF, and specifically SAF, is progressing on this front?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: As I have said quite a few times, the need to address climate change requires a whole-of-Government approach.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: MINDEF’s contributions towards this national effort to address environmental sustainability is no less important.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, climate change is more than an environmental issue as it has implications for our defence and security.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For small island nations like ours, the potential threats from rising sea levels and more volatile weather conditions can pose as much of a threat or, worse, compromise our national security measures.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Unfortunately, we have limited means to control the outcomes of global climate action.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Yet, the potential threat and damage to us from climate change are disproportionately large.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Nevertheless, when it comes to climate change mitigation, we will do our part and put in our best efforts.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We will continue to cooperate with global initiatives and collaborate with other governments, the private sector and non-profit organisations to mitigate climate change.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We need to pull together a whole-of-society effort to improve environmental sustainability.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: At the COS debate last year, the Minister for Defence spoke about the various measures taken by MINDEF and SAF to improve environmental sustainability and reduce carbon emissions.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Would the Ministry provide an update on these initiatives and how MINDEF/SAF has continued to contribute to national efforts to meet the objective of environmental sustainability?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One of the areas I am interested in is how MINDEF is working to meet our national targets to reduce energy and water consumption within its own buildings, bases and fleets, both in Singapore and overseas.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will SAF be tapping more into green technologies for greater energy efficiency?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will we see more military vehicles powered by green energy and do we see the infrastructure ready to support more of such vehicles which will help to reduce emissions?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Does MINDEF purchase carbon offsets and, if so, what was the quantum last year?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will MINDEF elaborate on its sustainability requirements for its procurements and how it processes the various categories of waste it generates?

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Singaporeans serving National Service Full-time, or NSFs, spend around two years in the SAF at a formative period in their lives.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: In this regard, it is important to provide support for our NSFs to contribute meaningfully during their service to our nation.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: This is an important initiative that would further harness the potential of our NSFs and also prepare a long, strong talent pipeline for specific industries.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Could the House be given an update on the WSD programme?

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: In addition, would we consider more of such schemes for Servicemen who may be interested to explore other careers?

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Many of our NSFs also take on other part-time courses on their own accord.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: To build on the current WSD programme, and possibly streamline NSFs personal learning efforts aligning with SAF’s needs, are there any plans for MINDEF to launch similar programmes for other vocations?

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: This matter of falling manpower is an issue that SAF has had to grapple with.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: In order to keep Singapore secure, it is critical to ensure that a leaner SAF can continue to maintain its capability edge and operational readiness, by maximising the use of its available manpower, while keeping ahead of our evolving landscape.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: However, some of our NSFs pick up new capabilities and competencies along their professional work life, some of which could be meaningfully leveraged by SAF in its move towards digital transformation, green technology and new capabilities.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: The level of physical fitness required in these roles differs from those in operational ones.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: A review in criteria may open up a larger talent pool for SAF to tap on these roles.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Chairman, your permission to take both cuts together.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Mr Chairman, training safety has been a key concern of mine for many years.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: This moment, I would also like to extend condolences to the 39-year-old Regular Serviceman who passed away unfortunately last week after undertaking personal physical training.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: It must and always be the SAF’s top priority.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: This is an obligation that the MINDEF and the Singapore Armed Forces owe to every Serviceman and their loved ones.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: The fresh perspectives from the diverse range of experts that were gathered on that panel would have provided the Singapore Armed Forces with insights on how to improve safety systems and processes.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Could the Minister provide an update on the panel’s findings and how has the SAF followed up on its recommendations?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Singaporean families send their children to serve in the SAF each year.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: The safety record of the SAF is naturally one of the key concerns of all families, and it is essential that we maintain the trust that Singaporeans have in the SAF.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: At the COS debate last year and in 2019 as well, the Minister for Defence Dr Ng and Senior Minister of State for Defence Mr Heng Chee How spoke about the SAF Inspector-General’s Office, or IGO in short, which plays a key role in strengthening safety in the SAF.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: I understand that the SAF IGO conducts audits of safety practices across the SAF.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Could the Minister provide an update on the IGO’s audit findings since 2019?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: And in light of this, what are the training safety measures that have been introduced in response to the IGO’s findings?

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: The healthcare sector is undergoing rapid digital transformation, from tele-medicine, the use of virtual reality in treatment, to wearable medical devices in preventive medicine.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: In the Senior Minister of State for Defence, Mr Heng Chee How’s speech at the COS debate last year, Senior Minister of State Heng highlighted that the SAF’s Virtual Care initiative as an example of how the SAF was leveraging technology to better serve our National Servicemen.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: This included the use of video conferencing tools to diagnose and prescribe treatment for common ailments remotely.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Mr Chairman, recently, the Straits Times reported on the findings of the State Coroner regarding the death of National Serviceman Dave Lee due to heatstroke, which was partially caused by delayed evacuation.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I cannot profess to know the pain of parents and families who have lost their loved ones.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: To quote the mother of Dave Lee, she said “Parents who have lost a child will never have any closure.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There will only be sadness...That is all I can say.” We know it is for an important cause.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The cost of our national defence has, however, fallen unevenly, with some families paying a higher price than others.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We should not take our people’s support for National Service for granted.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Apart from ongoing efforts to improve training safety, I would like to put forth two proposals for the Minister’s consideration.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: While I hate to put a price tag on the sacrifices made, ex-gratia payments based on WICA is, in my view, inadequate.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On this day, let the whole nation say to these families – we remember and we are grateful.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore's defence strategy is dependent largely on the contributions of our National Servicemen.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: It is important that should our soldiers suffer injuries in the course of their service to the nation, they will be fairly compensated.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will give them the assurance to give their best during training and operations.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I have a few questions for the Minister about MINDEF's insurance and compensation schemes.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: NSmen may be serving only up to 40 days a year, but they often participate in dangerous military exercises during that short stint.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Second, how was the amount for their insurance coverage derived?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Lastly, if a serviceman suffers a service injury in the course of actual combat operations, is the quantum of payouts the same as for training injuries?

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Chairman, all young male Singaporeans and residents have to commit two years in the prime of their lives for service to our nation.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: It is important that we recognise their contributions and sacrifices and do our best to support them as they prepare for further studies or entry into the workforce after they complete full-time NS.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: They may also need skills training or upgrading.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Does MINDEF have any form of referral arrangement with MSF?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Chairman, a capable and combat-fit SAF is the ultimate guarantor of Singapore's security and the physical fitness of our national servicemen is of utmost importance to the SAF's operational readiness.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The SAF has many long-standing policies aimed at encouraging physical fitness amongst our National Servicemen, such as requiring NSmen to pass IPPT annually and allowing NSFs to serve a shorter term of NS if they attain a high standard of physical fitness prior to enlistment.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: At the Committee of Supply debate last year, Senior Minister of State for Defence Mr Heng Chee How announced the PREP4NS initiative to help pre-enlistees be more physically prepared before entering NS.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: During this pandemic, the capacity of many MINDEF and civilian training facilities have been reduced due to safe distancing measures.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: What measures does MINDEF have in place to ensure that training venues, equipment and slots are accessible and available to our servicemen to keep fit and in shape?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The quality of food also has an impact on fitness.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Food insecurity may affect some servicemen in the lower income groups during this pandemic.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Does MINDEF provide any form of assistance to our servicemen to ensure that they have access to nutritious meals to stay healthy and fit?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Healthcare issues affecting our servicemen must be dealt with urgently and thoroughly as every manpower resource is precious.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Would the Ministry share an update on the healthcare measures and assistance schemes it has to keep our troops combat-fit?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: What else is MINDEF/SAF doing to better support and motivate our servicemen in maintaining their physical fitness?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: Chairman, one key focus area announced by the National Service Review Committee (NSRC) was to review aspects of NS to better meet the needs of a new generation of National Servicemen.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: MINDEF and the SAF must continue to be good stewards of our servicemen's time and talent.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: These are precious resources and should be utilised strategically.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: We have to adapt and seize the advantages presented by technological advancements.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: Proactive adaptation will enable us to be more efficient in our processes and also keep us ahead of emerging threats.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: Will there be improvements to waiting times and service delivery standards?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: In addition, it had been pointed out that there are trade-offs between convenience and security.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: What measures does MINDEF have in place to ensure that these processes are convenient, efficient and secure?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: Will the Ministry also share how regularly it collects and reviews feedback from NS servicemen and the public to enhance our NS processes?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Locally and globally, the COVID-19 pandemic has greatly amplified the role of technology in our lives.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: During the circuit breaker, the restrictions on movement increased our reliance on digital platforms and connectivity in multiple aspects of our lives.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: As Singapore embarks on a digitalisation journey, so must the SAF.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: On the defence front, how can we better tap on the opportunities presented by technology and digitalisation to improve the NS experience for all our servicemen and women?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: At MINDEF's Committee of Supply debate last year, I was glad to hear from Senior Minister of Stare for Defence Mr Heng Chee How's sharing on various technology and digital solutions that MINDEF/SAF had been working on to enhance different facets of the NS experience, from administration and training to healthcare.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Could MINDEF provide updates on how it is leveraging technology to enhance soldiers' NS experience and well-being?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Does MINDEF/SAF plan to integrate these different services, in order to provide our servicemen with a smoother and more convenient user experience?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Chairman, the strength of our Total Defence depends on every Singaporean playing his or her part to help our country overcome and emerge stronger from each crisis.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Singaporeans have put Total Defence into action to overcome past crises, such as the outbreak of SARS as well as economic downturns and terrorism threats.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic is an unprecedented test of our collective resilience as a nation.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It is heartening how Singaporeans have risen to the occasion to play their part in their fight against this COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Our people have banded together through adversity despite the uncertainties of the situation and personal hardships.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Singaporeans have much to be proud of our response to COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Yet, the fight is far from over and we must not let our guard down.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Mr Chairman, the send-off to Tekong, a common rite of passage for most Singaporean males, are often met with emotional farewells.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We see proud fathers, crying mothers, siblings with their smartphones out documenting the occasion.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The security of Singapore is contingent not only on the efforts of MINDEF and the SAF but also on the unwavering commitment of Singaporeans to defence.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Since its inception, the Advisory Council on Community Relations in Defence, ACCORD, had set out to deepen engagement with businesses, educational institutions, family members and community groups, as well as to facilitate initiatives from the community that better support National Defence and National Service (NS).

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Since then, the solidarity shown by the community with our soldiers has been heartwarming.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: More are aware of the sacrifices made by our soldiers and how it is imperative that we have Singaporeans defend Singapore.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Mr Chairman, we would like to seek updates from the Government about ACCORD's plans for the current term, 2020 to 2022, regarding efforts to strengthen community support for defence and NS.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What are the roll-out plans like, in terms of engagement, particularly for divisions like Punggol Town, where we have many young families with their sons going off to serve their country?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: With increasing use of the Internet and social media, many of us are becoming more vulnerable to fake news and misinformation online.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: Amidst the on-going pandemic, the spread of fake news has been an area of deep concern, especially given the potential for this to cause unnecessary alarm or panic, or lead Singaporeans to make misinformed choices relating to their health.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mr Chairman, I had raised this at last year's Committee of Supply and also recently spoken on this at the Motion on climate change.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Climate change poses a grave threat to Singapore and needs to be addressed in a concerted response by the whole-of-Government and society.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This is the third time I am raising this issue and I understand that some things do take time to work through.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It took me six consecutive years, bringing up the issue of paternity leave before it was finally approved.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Of course, it was raised by other Members of Parliament as well.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Like climate change, I play the long game!

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: So, let us place climate change as the seventh pillar of Total Defence and give it the priority and urgency that it deserves.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Chairman, in 1984, the Government recognised that national security was a massive and complex issue.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: We identified five pillars of Total Defence to acknowledge that areas, such as social cohesion and economic resilience, were as important as military strength.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Today, climate change is perhaps the most pressing concern for the world.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Rising sea levels and extreme weather conditions, amongst other climate change threats pose ever-increasing dangers to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Climate change also have a big impact on our military operations and training, the maintenance of equipment and facilities and the direction of future defence strategies.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: The climate change threat needs to be addressed by a concerted response by the whole-of-Government and society.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: In this Budget, we have made room for long-term planning, including for environmental issues.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: If the Ministry does so, environmental defence will be front and centre in our defence schemes.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: As part of our national security planning, there will be implications for policies, national priorities, resource allocation and long-term environment defence strategies.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Having Climate Defence as the seventh pillar of Total Defence will send a powerful message to all Singaporeans and the world about how seriously we are tackling climate change and our level of commitment to environmental sustainability.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Going forward, this consideration will underpin all major decisions we make and facilitate more effective defence coordination.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: I urge the Ministry to consider this suggestion seriously.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, permission to take both of my cuts together.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Chairman, Since its introduction in 1984, Total Defence has played an important role in our society.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: It was recognised early on that threats, not just military threats, will impact Singaporeans from all walks of life.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Ensuring that Singapore is safe and secure is not simply the duty of MINDEF and the SAF, and it is truly a whole-of-nation effort.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: It is important that all Singaporeans are involved in conversations about Total Defence and about defence issues that impact everyone's lives, including National Service.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: This past year has been challenging for all of us and I have been heartened to see Singaporeans from all walks of life step up and help each other through difficult times.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: In light of the difficulties that we are faced with in the midst of this pandemic, I am interested to hear what Singaporeans had to say about keeping Singapore safe and secure and about how to strengthen Total Defence and NS.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Today, the COVID-19 crisis has tested Total Defence and the collective strength and unity of our society.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: We had to strike a balance between ensuring sufficient medical supplies, defending the nation from external dangers and protecting our relations with other countries.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: As Singapore works towards emerging stronger from this crisis and adapting ourselves to a post-COVID-19 world, Total Defence will remain indispensable to a united Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: However, the success of Total Defence is contingent upon active participation and engagement by all parts of society, including the Government, businesses, communities and individuals.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: COVID-19 has made all the more evident that we must continue to build resilience in our people and community.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: In order for Singapore to prevail over other existential threats to come, it is important that we fortify the resilience of the entire community.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: First, let me thank Members of this House for their comments, their input, their feedback and their positive comments about the SAF's contribution to this fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: My MINDEF colleagues, Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How and Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad and I are very thankful for these comments.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I am sure our senior officials and commanders will be greatly encouraged by your positive comments.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As Members of House have eloquently described in their speeches, this year's Committee of Supply and Budget Debates are being held in truly extraordinary circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Mr Alex Yam, Miss Cheng Li Hui, Ms Joan Pereira talked about this.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: To wit, COVID-19, a once-in-a-century disruptive change agent, has become the defining issue of our time, with its spread to all corners of our world.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Rustle through the pages of history and very few epochal events have had that kind of impact.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I think, World Wars One and Two, certainly; the advent of the steam engine, electricity, the telegraph and the Internet.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But those changes evolved over decades, not precipitously.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Just barely a year later and our lifestyles have been changed – here and everywhere, some turned upside down.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Singapore needed one circuit breaker, but many countries had two, three, even four or more imposed to contain this dreaded disease.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Experts think that the post-COVID-19 world will never revert to status quo ante.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: A new normal beckons and it is to this future for which we must prepare and position Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The phrase "never waste a good crisis" comes to mind.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I will share during this Committee of Supply the lessons we are learning from the pandemic and the adjustments, even new directions, that MINDEF and the SAF will take.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Our traditional security challenges remain and I will provide updates of those plans, but we must also deal decisively with additional threats on the horizon.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But more importantly, how does Singapore prepare for the security environment of a post-COVID-19 world?

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Many Members of Parliament have talked about and asked	rightly – Dr Wan Rizal, Mr Abdul Samad, Mr Desmond Choo, Mr Shawn Huang.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The pandemic stress-tested the existing global system and not all components will survive unscathed.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It was already deteriorating before COVID-19 struck, but change of US administrations notwithstanding, the rivalry has in fact sharpened as a result of COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Instead of global co-operation, the geopolitical landscape became more fragmented.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: You could draw a coloured map of the world based on the vaccines they are using, whether produced in the United States, Europe, Russia, China or India.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Mr Chairman, can I ask that the map be distributed.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This is the map that MINDEF staff came up with.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I think it will be too much of a stretch to say that this will be the world henceforth but these "vaccine blocs" – blue, red or multi-coloured – are instructive about affiliations and even directions in our future.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Vaccine diplomacy, as we see it, can extend to other systemic levers too.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It has already involved technology, namely 5G, semi-conductor chips, but other areas like debt financing, supply chains, purchase of arms and defence equipment are up for grabs.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It is difficult to conceive of a wholly-bifurcated world but neither will the post-COVID-19 world be a rainbow-coloured one hoped for, à la Globalisation 1.0.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Since 9/11, now two decades old, the United States and its allies have been committing resources and troops to the Middle East.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This generation will witness a shift of hard assets to our region in Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Previous US defence secretaries have progressively committed more assets to the Indo-Pacific area.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The United Kingdom has declared that it would send a carrier strike group to the South China Sea this year.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I do not need to embellish these trends as Members of this House can readily imagine the potential consequences from the increasing militarisation in Asia, both from countries within and outside.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: MINDEF's response to the heightened contestation is to remain friends with all.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We continue to work with like-minded partners to forge a security architecture that is inclusive for big or small countries and in which disputes are resolved through peaceful means.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We encourage countries to dialogue, cooperate and respect a rules-based international order.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This is a motherhood statement of policy, but as Members here can well imagine, the actual implementation can be difficult and tricky.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For Singapore's voice to be heard amid the cacophony, we must be useful to stronger voices, especially when tensions rise.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Members would have read of our many interactions with other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Bilaterally, apart from strong relationships with both the United States and China, we are friends with many countries in areas of mutual interest.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Some recent examples: with Australia, our Prime Minister signed the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: With India, we signed agreements to enhance collaboration in humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, and submarine rescue support and cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We also inaugurated the Singapore-India-Thailand Maritime Exercise in 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Apart from the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting Plus (ADMM-Plus) this year, we will commemorate the 50th anniversary of the Five Power Defence Arrangements, which remain strategically important to the regional security architecture.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Another signature security event that achieves this is the Shangri-La Dialogue.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We had to cancel it in 2020 last year but this year, it is on track to being held physically, barring unforeseen circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: These engagements are not merely good to have but necessary to protect our interests.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: MINDEF and the SAF will step up these efforts even as contestation increases.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Another epiphany from this COVID-19 pandemic is that we must continue to plan long term and, more importantly, steadily invest in emerging and novel capabilities precisely when we think we least need them.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I think this was Mr Alex Yam's point.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Nowhere has this wisdom been more vindicated than in MINDEF and SAF's ability to respond to COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I do not want this House to misunderstand.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This is not hubris speaking but deep gratitude for the commitment to defence spending over many years.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The virus first entered Singapore at the end of January 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: At the same time, general staff, with medical input from SAF Medical Corps' doctors, had to ensure continuity of operations.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Through the waves of infections last year, and despite on-going SAF operations – apart from the brief suspension of basic military training (BMT) during the circuit breaker – only a small number of COVID-19 cases arose within the SAF.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: They were detected, contained effectively, with no clusters formed.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Mass testing by DSO for SAF soldiers, practical medical advice for cohorting and other safety measures were key weapons and confidence boosters in our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: DSO has gone on to improve PCR and antigen testing.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Within MINDEF and the SAF, DSO and the Medical Corps validated that saliva tests are shown to be as accurate as nasal swabs.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As a result, the SAF has been using saliva tests to complement swab tests for monitoring of its soldiers since October last year.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The RESOLUTE 2.0 PCR kits were also essential in dealing with the outbreaks in the migrant worker community.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Apart from PCR and antigen testing, serological testing of large numbers was needed to prevent our community care facilities and quarantine facilities from being overwhelmed.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The Medical Corps and DSO staff worked with MOH to validate serological tests.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: At its peak, the joint taskforce worked with MOH to test nearly 40,000 sometimes, each week.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In March last year, DSO bio-staff harvested convalescent plasma from our COVID-19 patients here, then isolated and identified their neutralising antibodies.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: These antibodies are starting clinical trials with Government agencies, research institutes and biomedical companies.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The key question is: “Where did this bio-defence and medical capability come from and how was it maintained?” The answers are simple: people and facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: After SARS, we did not let that crisis go to waste, learnt the right lessons, built more secure bio-labs in DSO.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Quietly and without fanfare, this group of men and women has stayed true to their mission.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Our capabilities against chemical threats have also been strengthened.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Few Singaporeans know that DSO is a designated lab by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW).

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: OPCW is the leading international organisation, 193 member states, that heads investigations when toxic substances are suspected to be present.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The fact that DSO is designated as part of this network speaks highly of our standards and competence internationally, not to mention the resources we would have locally if ever such an episode occurred in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The current Laboratory Head of OPCW, this is based in The Hague, Ms Chua Hoe Chee, is the first Singaporean to be appointed to this role.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Members would agree with me that those investments from our defence budget that went into building medical and scientific capabilities have paid for themselves many times over.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Had we not learnt the right lessons following SARS, sarin, anthrax and other lethal chemical and biological incidents over the years, DSO would not have had the facilities, let alone the people and expertise to produce tests and other breakthroughs, when COVID-19 invaded our shores.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As an infectious agent, COVID-19 could have been much worse.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For example, mumps and measles are four to nine times more infectious.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For lethality, SARS and MERS caused many more severe cases and deaths.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Suppose we are unlucky, and we get a virus that is just as infectious as mumps and measles, and just as lethal as SARS and MERS.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Can we plan on the basis that future pandemics or biological attacks will not be worse than COVID-19?

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Or can we “outsource” to or call another country for help when it happens?

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I think Members in this House would unanimously say surely not.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It would be foolish to depend on others and we need to build capabilities within Singapore to protect ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Many developed countries already have labs with the highest biosafety level – we call these BSL-4.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Since 2015, countries in Asia like China, Japan and Korea have also built these BSL-4 labs.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Singapore has BSL-3 labs, which prior to this pandemic, were assessed as adequate protection.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The BSL-4 labs will require more stringent levels of air separation and must have the ability to quickly shut down and isolate that facility, when needed.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It goes without saying that safety is paramount, and DSO will work with MOH to ensure that we will have the highest standards of protection required for BSL-4 labs.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will bring in third-party and overseas experts to advise us on the entire process – beginning from the design, to construction and thereafter, to validate the systems periodically.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will maintain our record of absolute safety of our bio-labs built so far.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: There is another area in which steady investments paid rich dividends – our ability to exercise command and control over complex operations.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: They included packing five million masks in two days, stabilising the outbreak in the foreign worker dormitories, helping set up the Community Care and Recovery Facilities, supporting contact tracing and medical logistics operations.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Senior SAF commanders assumed leadership of several national taskforces, reporting to the Multi-Ministry Task Force.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: DSTA developed command and control systems for the national COVID-19 operations.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: These smooth operations occurred because this is what the SAF does, day in day out.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: All of us here who have served our National Service and In-Camp Trainings know this.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We may grumble sometimes about these mobilisations as NSmen, but it keeps the machinery warm, so that when the SAF is activated, it ramps up into the lean and mean machine it needs to be.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Even as the SAF contributed to the fight against COVID-19, it continued to maintain operations at a high level of readiness to keep Singapore safe from external threats.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And Mr Alex Yam talked about this in his cut.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Protection of key installations, maritime security, air defence, counter-terrorism efforts continued around the clock.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: On training, which some members have asked about, some overseas and large-scale exercises like the RSAF’s Darwin detachment and the multilateral naval exercise RIMPAC have resumed, enabled by strict adherence to safe management measures, robust testing, and enhanced medical protocols.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Others will take time to restart or reach pre-COVID levels.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The nation-wide vaccination programme will facilitate this resumption.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: There have been questions asked about RSAF training.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And I have addressed questions on RSAF training in this House last year as she had pointed out, which were put forth by Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and Dr Lim Wee Kiak.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I do not intend to reprise those remarks, which Members can look up in the Hansard.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I will give an update on RSAF training this year.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The impact of COVID-19 was precipitous and to keep our fighter pilots current, the number of local training flights increased in 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We had to call on the generosity and goodwill of foreign partners so that more of our pilots can train overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Please be reminded that they too have local populations in overseas training detachments, perhaps not as densely populated as Singapore, but communities there will have to bear with the noise generated by our planes.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I want to thank the defence establishments and communities of these countries for helping us build our capabilities to defend Singapore – they are true friends.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: With their help, the RSAF local training this year will be brought down to pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But let me sound a gentle note of caution.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We have good friends overseas, but if for any reason – whether it is a worsened COVID-19 outbreak or complaints from their local community – Singaporeans must be prepared for local training to be stepped up.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The SAF will do all it can to minimise this, but Singaporeans must be willing to make some sacrifices for our own security.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Mr Desmond Choo, Mr Shawn Huang have asked for updates on the development of the Next Generation SAF.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For the Army, Headquarters Sense and Strike was inaugurated last November.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This is essentially a re-organisation of HQ Army Intelligence and HQ Singapore Artillery under 6 Division, to integrate capabilities so that both can “See Better” and “Shoot Faster” with less manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We also inaugurated the Navy’s Maritime Security and Response Flotilla, made up of refurbished patrol vessels.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Four new purpose-built vessels will replace them in due course.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The RSN will also deploy unmanned surface vessels and complete their sea trials later this year to complement manned ships for maritime security.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For the RSAF, upgraded F-16s are expected to roll out in the coming months.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Shawn Huang made very incisive remarks about how we should not be distracted by COVID-19 against existing threats.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The terrorist groups in the Middle East, particularly Al-Qaeda and ISIS, have been weakened.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But paradoxically, success there can increase the threat here especially when the number of terrorists coming into our region has gone up, either returning or foreign, bringing with them networks, tactics and expertise in violent crimes and explosives.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Our concern is that the collective intelligence and surveillance capability of ASEAN is a fraction of what the US and allies have in the Middle East.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The CTIF will bring together like-minded countries to share intelligence, provide early warning, monitoring and analysis capabilities in a centralised and coordinated manner.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Mr Shawn Huang and Miss Rachel Ong asked about emerging areas, technology and the like.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We are already employing artificial intelligence, robotics and data analytics to enable new warfighting concepts and force multipliers for the Next Gen SAF.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: MINDEF has also recently established a “Digital Factory”.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It allows our people, product developers and designers to come together under one roof, to collaborate on designing, testing and scaling secure digital solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And as a result, we have been able to build and deploy software three times faster than before.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The Cloud will play a greater role in our digital future.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But for defence establishments, there will always be security concerns as we move to cloud-based systems.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Nevertheless, after careful study, MINDEF and the SAF have decided that cloud computing is a key component to enhance effectiveness and reduce our need for manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: These were the points touched on by Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Mr Patrick Tay.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Beyond this, classified information will also leverage cloud systems.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This was a big decision, after much study and debate.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As the security standards for these areas need to be more stringent, such systems will be physically housed in MINDEF/SAF and separated from other day-to-day functions on the cloud.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked about the Integrated Cyber Command Force.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This has improved our ability to monitor and actively seek out potential threats and aggressors in the cyber domain.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We have already announced that more NSmen will serve in the CSTF and we are working with academic institutions to raise their skills through initiatives, such as the University Work-Learn Programme with NUS and the Critical Infrastructure Security Showdown cybersecurity exercises – I am not sure this is showdown or shutdown but it says "showdown" here – with SUTD's iTrust Centre for Research in Cyber Security.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I think this is something that Miss Rachal Ong mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As our platforms in the SAF evolve to run on new technology and as we add new roles, such as cyber-specialists and drone operators, indeed, more opportunities are created for our NSmen; and a number of Members of Parliament have made this point.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And they reminded us that last year, I announced the set-up of the NS Review Committee headed by our Chief of Army and MINDEF's Deputy Secretary for Administration.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How will provide an update in his speech shortly.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But let me address points asked by Mr Chong Kee Hiong, Mr Mohd Fahmi and Mr Shawn Huang that with more jobs redesigned and using new technology, indeed, a larger pool of servicemen will now be able to contribute in areas for which they were previously not eligible or capable.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And this has less to do with our manpower constraints but the expansion of capabilities and avenues in which they can contribute.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For example, being deployed for maritime security and protection of installations, through the use of unmanned surface vessels and unmanned watch towers.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: More fundamentally, the NS Review Committee has highlighted that the old binary classification that many of us grew up with here of Combat-Fit or non-Combat-Fit – makes little sense when applied to roles such as unmanned vessel operators.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Miss Rachel Ong used another term – "operational" and "non-operational".

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: That also does not capture what we are talking about because an unmanned vessel operator has very little to do whether he is combat-fit or not combat-fit.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, the old system is outdated and retrogressive for many roles in the Next Gen SAF.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The new system will take into account their civilian jobs and skillsets which Members of Parliament have asked about.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Of course, these changes must not compromise safety or the operational readiness of the SAF.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As I have said, Senior Minister of State Mr Heng Chee How will give more details.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng, Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Don Wee asked about climate change and sustainability and I would like to touch on this last topic.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I spoke about some changes MINDEF and the SAF were already making at last year's Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And since then, the Government has unveiled the Singapore Green Plan 2030 (SGP30), a whole-of-nation movement to advance Singapore's national agenda on sustainable development.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And rightly, Members of Parliament have asked what is MINDEF and SAF's response and involvement in SGP30.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: After all, it would be understandable, perhaps even excusable, given our mandate, to reduce our commitment or even opt out.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I want to assure this House that MINDEF and SAF will more than do our part for SGP30.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The COVID-19 vaccine was developed in the fastest time in human history – never seen before.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: What used to take years to accomplish was done in weeks.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In fact, a few days the mRNA sequence was produced after the genome came out.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But the consequences of extreme climate change are existential and cannot be mitigated, let alone solved, in weeks, months, even years.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will have three major green initiatives – carbon emissions, water and waste – with key targets for the SAF to go greener.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Today, our main sources of emissions are building infrastructure and military platforms – no surprise there.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: These changes are significant and will reduce our carbon emissions growth by about 40% by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For platforms, it is harder to reduce emissions, but we will do so when replacements are available and cost-effective, without any loss of operational effectiveness, compromise in security or sharp rise in defence spending.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will do so when replacements are available and cost effective, without any loss of operational effectiveness, compromise in security or sharp rise in defence spending.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I choose my words carefully, not to over-promise unrealistic goals, but neither to evade responsibility to show results but we will do what we can.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The Army will replace its current administrative vehicle fleet with an all-electric one by 2030 – 400 of them.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In tandem, charging infrastructure in camps and bases will be set up.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The RSN will equip newer vessels like the Littoral Mission Vessels with energy-efficient LED lights, ozone-free water-mist fire suppression systems and look into using garbage converters to reduce waste volume.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For air combat platforms, green fuels that meet the criteria of cost effectiveness are just not yet fully developed.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Nevertheless, the RSAF will commence trials of green aviation fuel for some of our F-16s, so that we can understand the engineering, logistics and infrastructure works needed to scale up its use when these green fuels do become more cost effective.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will take further steps to reduce water consumption.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will progressively replace water fittings with more efficient ones which are at least three-ticks under the Water Efficiency Labelling Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will continue to invest in water recycling systems, such as those for vehicular washing.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The goal is a 10% reduction in water consumption by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
