text: We will step up the "3Rs – Reduce, Reuse and Recycle" initiative significantly.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For food waste, we have already implemented segregation and recycling processes in 14 cookhouses.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will extend this to all cookhouses by 2024.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We have put in place waste disposal contracts to recycle and repurpose electronic waste, waste oil, chemicals and scrap metal.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The aim is to reduce waste by 30% by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: To succeed in this SAF-wide initiative, we must empower all units to contribute their best efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: When the smart metering is complete, unit commanders will be equipped to compare themselves with their peers and benchmarks and to reach their required targets.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I must add that MINDEF and SAF are able to do this because we have direct command and control over all our units.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This initiative to go greener needs to be sustained for the long-term and Mr Seah Kian Peng calls it a "long game".

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But it can be derailed by a few forces.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Apathy and lack of awareness are two that I hope will be alleviated by the use of smart meters.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But there is another force that can dissipate our efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: If each group champions its favourite environmental cause, the SAF could be pulled in different and sometimes, unproductive directions.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, MINDEF and the SAF must start off on and maintain the correct trajectory, guided by science, data and evidence on effective outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We must put in a structure to achieve these outcomes and not get distracted along the way.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I believe that this command structure guided by the right advice will put us in the best possible trajectory for this long-term enterprise.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: My colleagues Senior Ministers of State Heng Chee How and Zaqy Mohamad will address other points which Members have brought up.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Mr Chairman, I want to conclude on two points.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The clarion cry that we have heard in this House again and again, indeed, for this generation of Singaporeans facing this globally destructive and disruptive COVID-19 pandemic, is to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For MINDEF/SAF, we must, if we are to secure our defence for another generation.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Much of what I have talked about is looking far ahead, to a future in which we continue to have an SAF that can protect Singapore's interests and the well-being of Singaporeans despite the uncertainty and rising risks in our region and globally.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I am deeply conscious, Mr Chairman and Members of this House, that defence takes up a sizeable share of the Government budget and not just the resources of our Budget but more importantly, he personal commitment of the servicemen and their families, something Ms Joan Pereira and Ms Hazel Poa talked about.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I want to thank Members of this House and Singaporeans for your trust, your unstinting support and commitment to maintain a strong defence.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: All MINDEF and SAF can offer in return to you and the Singaporeans that we serve is this pledge to be good stewards of these investments and to keep Singapore safe for many years ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chairman, Defence Minister Dr Ng has emphasised the need for a forward-looking SAF to confront increasingly complex challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As the SAF adapts to face these challenges, National Service or NS must be a crucial part of this transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As the Minister for Defence has described just now, with differing medical fitness levels, education backgrounds and skillsets, our servicemen can contribute to our defence effectively but differently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We seek to unlock their potential in several ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: First, establishing new vocations and redesigning existing ones for our full-time national servicemen, or NSFs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In recent years, new vocations have been established in the SAF in response to the changing threat environment, such as the vocation of cyber specialists who protect our networks and systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For more established roles, the Minister for Defence has highlighted our redesign of jobs through technology, such as the development of unmanned watchtowers and unmanned surface vessels to augment our security troopers and base defence operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Second, better matching of servicemen to roles where they can be operationally effective, regardless of medical fitness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: That system has been with us for a long time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Medical exclusions that used to limit deployments may no longer be so relevant in today's operational context, especially with the latest technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The key idea is to deploy every soldier in a meaningful operational role without compromising safety and while maintaining and ensuring operational effectiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are therefore reviewing the use of functional assessments to determine our servicemen's deployability in specific vocations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For example, the SAF has introduced functional assessments to guide our selection of transport operators – just as a practical example.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: What that assessment does is that it replicates the physical demands required for daily operations, enabling us to better match our servicemen's functional abilities to the role's actual demands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: If successful, we will then extend this trial to other vocations such as tank operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In other words, we look at the vocations – the jobs – and the requirements of those jobs as opposed to whether you are rated combat-fit or not combat-fit and then try to fit our servicemen into those two categories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Third, helping our servicemen acquire new skills to better perform their roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked about the Work-Study Diploma, or WSD, which we launched last September with the Institute of Technical Education (ITE).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As a start, this is open to NSFs serving as Air Force and Army technicians.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Under the WSD, servicemen will undergo training to obtain a MINDEF-sponsored ITE diploma in Aircraft Maintenance Engineering or Electrical Engineering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Spending three or four years in total with the SAF, these servicemen will be given a contract that will entitle them to the pay and benefits of an SAF Regular after they have completed a stipulated period as NSFs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These WSDs are MINDEF and the SAF's latest addition to "work-learn" schemes for our full-time national servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We also introduced the Cyber NSF Scheme in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These schemes support our servicemen's professional development while allowing them to put their learning into practice and contribute to MINDEF and the SAF in the defence of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will continue to explore more of such "work-learn" schemes in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Beyond NSFs, we see a valuable opportunity to harness the useful knowledge and skills that our NSmen have attained through their studies and civilian work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In 2019, we announced that NSmen with specialised civilian expertise can be deployed earlier in their Operationally Ready NS cycle earlier to areas requiring such expertise, such as in law and psychology, under the Expertise Conversion Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The scheme has served us well against a growing spectrum of non-conventional threats, including in domains such as infocommunications and maritime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Even as we seek to maximise our servicemen's contributions to mission success, let me at the same time emphasise that safety will always be a central priority for us as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It is always mission success and safety always.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Following the training accidents from 2017 to 2019, the SAF has invested even more significant efforts to enhance safety management in our units, to train our commanders better in safety leadership and to establish an even stronger safety culture among our soldiers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The second ERPSS completed their 3.5-year tenure in December 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: They have been extremely helpful to MINDEF and the SAF in assessing the progress of the SAF's safety journey as well as in highlighting opportunities for improvement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We also appreciate all the Panel members' participation in the MINDEF's Committee of Inquiry (COI) for training accidents and the Panel's independent review of all COI findings on training safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked about the second ERPSS' findings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The second ERPSS acknowledged the efforts and progress the SAF has made to strengthen safety and observed its strong command emphasis on building a positive safety culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These efforts include internalising the importance of safety in SAF units' everyday activities and leveraging digital means to enhance safety management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The Panel also offered useful suggestions based on the industry's best practices such as benchmarking the safety training of our commanders, trainers and safety officers to those of the industry standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SAF will follow up on these recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Apart from the ERPSS, the SAF conducts internal audits to ensure there are robust safety management systems and a healthy safety culture in our units.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Overall, the IGO observed notable progress in strengthening the SAF's safety culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: There has been a sustained uptrend in open reporting received in the past two years, where servicemen, regardless of rank, reported near-misses and safety hazards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our units have also made significant adjustments to their training schedule to permit time for safety, including conducting daily safety briefs and catering dedicated training time to obtain feedback from soldiers on safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: To overcome the rank gradient, our units have appointed rank and file soldiers as safety advocates to communicate and facilitate communication with their unit's commanding officers on safety matters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The IGO's audits also found that soldiers have responded positively to the safety measures implemented in this past two years – building on past efforts but within the two years since the IGO's formation – with our commanders leading enhancements in unit safety processes and influencing their soldiers' safety mindsets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Nevertheless, given the constant turnover of servicemen, it is crucial that the SAF sustains these efforts, keeping our soldiers updated on the latest safety incidents and lessons learnt to avoid making mistakes or repeating mistakes and doing all we can to prevent accidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Ultimately, the SAF is committed to the vision of zero accidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We must continue to uphold our duty of care to every serviceman entrusted to us – as highlighted by the Minister for Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our attention to safety extends beyond training safety systems to ensuring our medical systems are progressively improved – which Miss Rachel Ong asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: After all, our servicemen's health is paramount to their safety and their well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In collaboration with the DSTA and industry partners, we have developed a portable electronic medical records system – or what we call PACES Mobile.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This enables our medical officers to access our servicemen's medical information remotely on their laptops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: By providing our medical officers with the full medical history of our servicemen, including while they are on overseas exercises and deployments, PACES Mobile has improved medical safety and the quality of patient care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: MINDEF and the SAF will spare no effort to protect our servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Yet, the reality is that every military force around the world will have to deal with the prospect of injury and death amongst its soldiers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked about our care for soldiers who suffer service injuries and Ms Hazel Poa, the recognition for servicemen who die in service and the support given to their families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our compensation framework takes reference from but goes beyond what is provided for by the Work Injury Compensation Act, or WICA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: MINDEF will also pay for all necessary medical expenses of injured servicemen at Government restructured hospitals, clinics and community hospitals for as long as it is required.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This includes the cost of medical supplies, counselling and specialist care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Again, this exceeds WICA's provisions, where the compensation for loss of earnings is up to a year from the date of the accident.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Over and above all these, MINDEF provides servicemen with life and personal accident insurance during their term of service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Beyond compensation, injured servicemen may also receive financial assistance under MINDEF's welfare schemes, which can assist with immediate needs, depending on family circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Other forms of support are also provided based on the serviceman's and his family's specific needs, including medical arrangements and counselling support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These avenues of support extend also to the families of our deceased servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: That said, no amount of compensation or assistance can replace a loved one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: And that is why we take the trust that Singaporeans and Singaporean families have in MINDEF and the SAF absolutely seriously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will do everything we can to look after our servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It carries immense significance for the family and we in MINDEF and the SAF certainly honour our fallen men and women.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Ms Hazel Poa spoke of dedicating a day to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It is called the SAF Day and we have a parade every year in the presence of our President or our Prime Minister.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In the course of that parade, we remember specifically men and women of the SAF who have fallen in the course of duty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Individual units and formations also hold remembrance events to honour their men and women who have fallen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our servicemen serve a critical operational need and we greatly value their contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Yet, we recognise that beyond serving the nation, our servicemen are also critical contributors to their families, some of whom face economic dislocation, for example, last year, due to the disruption brought on by COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Commanders have been paying special attention to signs of financial distress among NSFs during the pandemic, and where necessary and appropriate, have helped with the application for such financial assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The assistance schemes have, therefore, been deployed in tandem with the evolving economic situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The application process has been simplified and shortened, and we also allow for more extensions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Don Wee also asked about the support available to NSFs anxious about entering a difficult job market after full-time NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Under SkillsFuture@NS, NSFs can use their Electronic Pre-Release Employment Programme, or E-PREP credits, for over 4,000 selected courses to update or acquire new skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We also organise a quarterly Enhanced Career and Education Fair, where NSFs can access resources on career and educational opportunities and attend customised SkillsFuture Advice workshops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In addition, we have enhanced their Certificate of Service package to reflect not only our NSFs’ achievements and contributions, but also their competencies gained through Workforce Skills or WSQ Qualifications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This serves as a useful reference for prospective employers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We constantly seek to motivate our servicemen to keep fit and healthy, as this forms a good foundation upon which to build our SAF’s operational capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For pre-enlistees, I introduced the Pre-Enlistees Exercise Programme for NS, or PREP4NS, last year, where pre-enlistees can register for complimentary one-year membership to six SAFRA gyms to improve their fitness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: More than 80% of these have visited the SAFRA gyms since mid-June last year, notwithstanding the difficulties posed by COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Quite obviously, if not for COVID-19, the response would be even greater.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Many have also reported improvements in their Individual Physical Proficiency Test (IPPT) scores.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are expanding the PREP4NS trial to include admission, beyond the SAFRA gyms, to 24 ActiveSG gyms across Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Pre-enlistees can look forward to yet more facilities to prepare for Basic Military Training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Registration for the PREP4NS membership to the ActiveSG gyms will be announced later.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Similarly, we are mindful of the work-life demands on our NSmen’s time and are exploring additional ways to provide more convenience and flexibility for NS fitness activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This will motivate our NSmen to keep an active lifestyle, ensuring that they remain operationally ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked about initiatives to make our NS processes more convenient for our servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Besides fitness activities, our enhanced Health Screening Programme (HSP) is a key example of this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: First, we can now complete the HSP for most NSmen in a single session instead of two, thus saving them an entire trip.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Second, we will establish a specialised HSP centre in our MMI campus in NUS Kent Ridge by mid-2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: MMI used to be known as the Military Medicine Institute.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This centralised location will bring greater convenience to our busy NSmen, who can expect shorter booking and waiting times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Better experience through digitalisation is the next area that I will speak on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The NSRC’s third focus area is enhancing every serviceman’s NS experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our daily activities are increasingly conducted on digital platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We therefore intend to leverage technology to enhance the NS experience, and this is part of our digital transformation efforts, which is on-going, and which the Defence Minister mentioned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: MINDEF and SAF have established an NS digital transformation plan for the next five years to develop digital products catering to our tech-savvy servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We also have plans to consolidate all digital services through the NS journey onto a single platform, which is what Mr Patrick Tay asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: With committed and capable national servicemen, Singapore will continue to more than survive and to thrive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With every Singaporean organisation, family and individual playing a part through Total Defence, we can deter threats, overcome crisis and emerge stronger from each test.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Member Dr Wan Rizal asked about how Total Defence played a part in Singaporeans’ fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our response to the pandemic is a good example of Total Defence in action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: COVID-19 has upended businesses and industries, affected jobs and disrupted the way we live.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SAF, the Public Service, the Home Team and many other agencies have worked hard to contain and manage the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our people have stepped up in support – from retired doctors and nurses to national servicemen, participating in COVID-19 operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Community and religious groups, volunteers and the everyday resident made efforts to reach out to those who are more affected, such as retrenched workers, lower income families and the elderly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Some even played their part to debunk misinformation and scaremongering on social media.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Working together has moderated the impact of COVID-19 and strengthened the resolve and cohesiveness of our society, not just in dealing with COVID-19, but for future threats too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is Total Defence in action – a demonstration of what we can achieve when the pillars of military, civil, economic, social, psychological and digital defence all working in concert.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In Total Defence, there are many everyday heroes and heroines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I have been privileged to meet many of them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One such person is full-time national serviceman (NSF) Lieutenant Karthikasan S/O Natarajan, an Air Warfare Officer from the Republic of Singapore Air Force (RSAF).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: During Karthikasan’s full-time National Service (NS), he volunteered to serve at the SAF-led Medical Operations Task Force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He meticulously verified the records of thousands of workers, ensuring that they would be transported, housed and cared for at the right facilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: What struck me about Karthikasan was his strong sense of duty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He extended his National Service commitments for eight months, so that he could continue to contribute to Singapore’s fight against COVID-19 and watch over Singapore’s skies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Another such person is Military Expert (ME) 4A (NS) Muhammad Nurhafiz Bin Juma’at, a 34-year-old Operationally Ready National Serviceman (NSman) from the Singapore Army’s 8th Combat Support Hospital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last year, Nurhafiz volunteered to serve as a Nursing Officer at the Singapore Expo Community Care Facility during his In-Camp Training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Nurhafiz took care of the migrant workers, pulling 12-hour shifts to ensure their well-being and facilitated their recovery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He even missed the first week of Hari Raya.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Nurhafiz said, and I quote, "The sacrifice was worth it as it was not only for our loved ones and the nation, but also to care for the migrant workers who are in need of our medical care and support during this critical period".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, Nurhafiz is a senior staff nurse at the Sengkang General Hospital and continues to contribute tirelessly at the frontline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These contributions, along with so many others, demonstrate how Singaporeans have gone beyond their call of duty to help others during this pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Every action, no matter how big or small, counts in our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, even as we focus on recovering and emerging stronger from COVID-19, we must remember the threats facing Singapore are never completely eliminated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We must therefore continue to emphasise Total Defence to prepare Singapore for the threats of today and tomorrow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Pillar by pillar, we must strengthen each of them so that they are even more ready and resilient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I echo Senior Minister of State Heng who shared our efforts to transform NS for the Next-Generation SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: NS is the foundation of our military defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As we continue to transform NS, we must continue to strengthen societal, business and family support for military defence and NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This way, we can continue to motivate our servicemen to do their best as they defend Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last year, I was pleased to welcome new members to the Advisory Council on Community Relations in Defence or what we know as ACCORD.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The new ACCORD is well-placed to provide fresh perspectives that will enhance its work to strengthen societal support for National Service and defence, with members that hail from diverse backgrounds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Council includes representatives from the banking, logistics, technology and e-commerce fields, such as new member, Mr Quek Siu Rui, CEO of Carousell, on board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: ACCORD also welcomes new members from youth-oriented organisations, such as Ms Tan See Leng, Executive Director of Heartware Network and Ms Samantha Ng, National Youth Council INSPIRIT Youth Leader.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Member of Parliament Yeo Wan Ling asked about the focus areas for the new ACCORD term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To enhance outreach, ACCORD is pushing for more digital engagement channels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MINDEF/SAF has begun working with ACCORD to put these new plans into action, and ACCORD members themselves have led some of these initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One example of digital engagement was a well-received webinar hosted last year by ACCORD Member and Director of Mums@Work, Mrs Sher-Li Torrey, for mothers with sons entering NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The mothers gained insights into what their sons can expect from NS and were assured that their sons would be well-taken care of.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They also provided useful feedback for us to consider.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will work with ACCORD to organise more of such webinars on a larger scale this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For parents whose sons are liable for NS, a visit to the Basic Military Training Centre (BMTC) is important to understand what their children will go through.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Due to COVID-19, such visits had to be temporarily discontinued.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In its place, from September last year, we piloted virtual visits to the BMTC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Many families said that the visit gave them a better understanding of NS training and felt that their sons' safety would be well-looked after.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MINDEF will soon expand these virtual BMTC visits to a wider group, including Singaporean families residing overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Besides going digital, we will develop other channels and more creative ways to engage Singaporeans on NS and Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The refreshed SDC will be a one-stop destination for visitors to learn and experience Singapore's history and imagine its future in a fun and immersive way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SDC re-opened partially last October, enabling visitors to experience the augmented reality (AR)-enhanced exhibits in the upper gallery that provide a cinematic journey into Singapore's history.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When the renovations are completed, SDC will unveil a refreshed lower gallery on contemporary issues confronting Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The public can look forward to more interactive features that encourage visitors to envision Singapore's future, through group activities, discussions and AR-enhanced exhibits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Visitors will go away with a better appreciation of what we are defending, against potential challenges confronting Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The SDC will also expand its outreach through new programmes for different groups, such as students, youths, National Servicemen and members of community organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: A new "Friends of SDC" volunteer group will also be formed to tap on the energies of volunteers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, individuals passionate about sharing our Singapore Story can sign-up as volunteer guides for the galleries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to strengthen all the pillars of Total Defence through collaboration with our partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Member of Parliament Patrick Tay had asked about Digital Defence, which was added two years ago.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have been working to strengthen Singapore's defences against cyber and disinformation attacks, which can be particularly damaging to our community, especially in crises like COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have collaborated with our partners to develop educational programmes on Digital Defence, to increase Singaporeans' understanding of digital threats and equip them with skills to detect and deal with fake news.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One such example is our collaboration with the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) to introduce the topic of Digital Defence in a module on Digital Transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through these programmes, we will continue to encourage actions that Singaporeans can take to be secure and responsible online, and strengthen our defences against online falsehoods that threaten to divide our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: There have been suggestions to add new Total Defence pillars, such as a biological defence pillar, or a climate defence pillar, as Members of Parliament Mr Seah Kian Peng and Mr Don Wee have suggested.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We agree that pandemics and climate change are both serious threats that require concerted responses by the Government, businesses, communities and individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We can take efforts on preparedness, actions and resilience in the physical, digital and psychological realms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Be it to address climate change or biological threats, we believe that the existing concept and pillars of Total Defence are relevant and can be put into action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: What is more important is that we act, and that our actions translate into impact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is why the Government has been strengthening our infectious disease infrastructure and we have just announced the Singapore Green Plan 2030 that we are all committed to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: On our part, MINDEF is fully committed in supporting these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Earlier, Dr Ng announced our plan to upgrade our facilities within the Defence Science Organisation (DSO) to the highest biosafety level, Biosafety Lab Level 4 (BSL-4), and MINDEF's efforts on environmental sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These are major moves that we are making within MINDEF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Member of Parliament Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked how MINDEF will support and empower more Singaporeans to play a greater role in Total Defence as we emerge from COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In these sessions that I attended, participants shared with me that COVID-19 had reinforced the importance of NS and Total Defence in preparing Singapore for crises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am heartened by their valuable suggestions to strengthen the public's commitment to NS and Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Their opinions demonstrate their determination and their will to shape Singapore’s future and protect its well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will hold more engagements this year to reach out to more people on NS and Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Member of Parliament Zhulkarnain asked about how MINDEF would take the outcomes of our public engagements forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are excited to embark on the suggestions raised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to end by quoting a thank-you note addressed to all National Servicemen who contributed to our COVID-19 operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Then a Primary 6 student from Nan Chiau Primary School, Miss Lin Yitong, wrote this note last year, and I quote, "Thank you, Mr Soldier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I appreciate everything you have done for the nation to fight the virus.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Let’s all stay strong and fight the virus!

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I echo Yitong's words of appreciation, determination and hope.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We thank our servicemen and every Singaporean for their contributions in the fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to build Total Defence into every Singaporean's DNA to meet the threats of today and tomorrow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Together, we will keep Singapore strong – for now, and for future generations to come.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Two quick clarifications, a follow up to my first cut.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Could I ask if Dr Ng could share more about the state of our bilateral and multilateral security relations with our immediate neighbours and key partners?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Are they on an even keel and does MINDEF see any potential downside in security cooperation in the region as the pandemic progresses?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: My second clarification is for Senior Minister of State Heng.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Could he share what proportion of units have already appointed them and if there are any significant ideas or improvements that have arisen from their participation?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Our agreements with India in terms of submarine rescue and the Singapore India-Thailand Maritime Exercise, or SITMEX, are emblematic of our trust; our agreements with China and the other Plus partners in the ASEAN Defence Ministers Meeting, or ADMM.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: With our surrounding countries, we have good relations with the Malaysian Armed Forces, as well as the TNI (Indonesian National Armed Forces) and we will continue to work with them.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But I think all of us are realistic.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We do not mean that there are no differences.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But from time to time, differences occur, and we will find channels to smooth over them and to continue to build ties.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, I would say that there are no spiky issues that we see on the horizon, but neither should we believe that it is all hunky-dory and, you know, we are all the best of pals.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I mean, it is, as I have said, the systemic risks have gone up and, in the contestation, whether it is between the US, China and other aspects, I think we can expect, from time to time, bumpy rides as well as the ability for the SAF to have to respond when we need to.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The hon Member Mr Alex Yam asked about the implementation status for the safety advocates in our services.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: I think this really goes to illustrate the seriousness with which we take the subject of safety and how we want to be open about it in order that we might be able to prevent accidents even better.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Chairman, I thank Senior Minister of State Heng for responding to my cut.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Can Senior Minister of State Heng clarify if operationally-ready NSmen who suffer service injuries or accidents will receive the same compensation and insurance coverage as full-time National Serviceman?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: If not, can MINDEF move towards this framework, given the invaluable contributions of our NSmen to our nation's defence?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Second, could SMS also share whether there are plans to increase the existing group term insurance coverage?

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: If I may request him to remind me of the third question that he had?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Is there a framework for enhanced coverage for servicemen who are killed or injured in action?

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Mr Chairman, the compensation framework relates to injuries suffered by servicemen in the course of their duty, in the course of training, in the course of service-related activities and, therefore, it would also cover actual operations.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Alex Yam, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Chairman, my thanks to fellow Members for the 41 cuts across a multitude of topics on our security and defence.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: A very big thank-you to Dr Ng Eng Hen, our two Senior Ministers of State, for their considered response and affirmation of our commitment towards safeguarding our sovereignty.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: With that, Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
